- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If model shows strong upward momentum after a recent dip (e.g., 3–5 consecutive rising forecasts), check for mean reversion; cap forecast at 1–2 standard deviations above recent mean.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid “sentiment mismatch” bias.
- When true outcome shows sharp reversal after a forecast peak, model often overshoots; apply lag correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast 3–5 days after peak.
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently forecasts higher than 20-day moving average, consider downward bias; adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
